chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman, and he learned after marrying her that she had committed adultery. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If her husband so desires, he can take the dower from the one who married her off, and for her is the dower in exchange for what she permitted of her chastity, and if he so desires, he may leave her.'

key_terms.الَّذِي زَوَّجَهَا: the one who married her off (matchmaker)

ai.seo_question: What are the husband's options regarding dower and divorce if his wife is found to have committed adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial rights in cases of pre-marital adultery, establishing that the wife retains her dower (sadaq) as compensation for the husband's enjoyment of her chastity, while the husband may optionally claim reimbursement from the matchmaker. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the dower is earned through the validity of the marriage contract and the husband's right to intimacy, rather than being strictly contingent on the wife's prior virginity or lack of prior sin. This ruling underscores the principle of 'sadaq bil-mustahall' (dower for what was made lawful), distinguishing between the contractual payment and potential damages from the third party.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Muawiya Bin Wahab who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who married a woman, so he came to know after marrying her that she had commited adultery. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If he so desires he can (stay) married to her and take the dower from the one who married her off, and for her is the dowry with what she had permitted from her chastity, and if he so desires to, he leaves her’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Mu‘awiyah ibn Wahab who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who marries a woman and afterwards finds out that she had committed fornication. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the husband wants he can take back from her guardian the mahr that he has paid, but she deserves the mahr because of which her marriage was made lawful, and if he wants he can separate from her (by means of divorce).”’
